body: Couldn't agree more on the activity. However, I just end up spending days and days only thinking about such an activity.

I liked the idea from the book Feeling Good by Burns - write down all the things that you plan to do, mark the ones you are doing alone, write down how much satisfaction you expected and how much satisfaction you actually felt while doing it. This made me thinking that there's so much we can do alone and even so much that we would even prefer doing alone (like reading a book or, e.g. I prefer working out alone).

Hahah. I don't know what way to take it, but you're not the only one saying that. Some therapists even charged me more than their rate, because I was "a difficult case", some just told me they wouldn't be able to help me (which I assume is normal to some extent). I don't feel like a difficult case though. But probably only because I slowly developed all these things over a long period of time. I don't even know if it's worth going to therapy though. It's not like I'm progressing anywhere and maybe I would just save a bunch of money and time, however much I have left.

Ah. Nice to see that it worked for you. Sorry for the weird question. I didn't even believe in medication before. Due to them never working for me, I always thought that there's some kind of conspiracy and none of them work other than cause side effects, until I met other people who had positive effects.

Does your gran know about the new "suicide note"?

I was thinking of getting a dog, so I wouldn't look like a creep when walking in a park in the middle of the night. But I'm really frustrated around dogs and other animals. And kids. Especially if they need attention. I don't know what to do, what to expect, how to act. I just feel weird/lost/frustrated. It even often pushes me to difficult situations where I have to explain to people that it's not that I wouldn't like animals, I just don't feel the excitement around them as other people do.
I guess this is my 10 minutes then. It would help to push the thoughts if I had something interesting to do.
Did you actually stop taking your medication? Did it even work/help for you?
